_doc: Registry of specialized fused-GDN-decode kernel integrations.  This
file IS the dispatch surface: it is consulted on every call and there
is no environment variable that turns it off.  Each row is one
complete gdn_fused_decode_step call signature served by one kernel
implementation; 'impl' names the module that serves it, next to this
file at kernel/gdn_fused_decode_<impl>.py.  A signature may appear
once per capable impl (this op ships two: a two-launch CuTe-DSL
kernel and a single-launch persistent CUDA kernel), and dispatch
prefers cute_dsl, then cuda, then the composable reference -- those
family names are internal, the op takes no backend argument.  New
kernels add impl modules and rows here; the dispatch code does not
change.
Signature fields: cc (SM as major*10+minor), b/hidden/n_ba/qkv_dim/
h_q/hv/d/conv_width/conv_state_len (exact sizes), conv_layout (the
physical conv-state pool layout: 'SD' = (state_len, dim) rows passed
as their transposed view -- the vLLM default -- or 'DS' = dense
(dim, state_len) rows).  Dtypes and stride patterns are fixed by the
op contract and checked by the dispatch guard, not per row.  Full
schema and the impl-module interface: README.md next to this file.
The layer geometry is a COMPILE-TIME PARAMETER of both impls, so a
new model geometry is new rows here plus a recompile, not new kernel
code.  Shipped surface on SM120, per impl:
hidden 5120, n_ba 96, qkv_dim 10240, 16 qk / 48 v heads, d 128,
conv width 4 -- decode batches 1/2/4/8;
hidden 2048, n_ba 64, qkv_dim 8192, 16 qk / 32 v heads, d 128,
conv width 4 -- decode batches 1/2/4.
Which checkpoints those rows are valid for: the first geometry was
captured from nvidia/Qwen3.6-27B-NVFP4 and the second from
nvidia/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-NVFP4, and each batch window comes from an
end-to-end serving sweep on that checkpoint.  A row matches
on its numbers and the device cc alone -- no row names a model and
nothing in the dispatch path reads one -- so any checkpoint whose
GDN layer has exactly these sizes dispatches here, and any that
differs anywhere falls through to the composable path.
A geometry must also satisfy the relations the kernels tile on
(n_ba == 2*hv, hv % h_q == 0, qkv_dim == (2*h_q + hv)*d, d == 128,
hidden and qkv_dim divisible by the CuTe-DSL K-split and conv tile);
the CUDA kernel static_asserts them and the CuTe-DSL impl checks them
at dispatch, so a bad row cannot silently mis-tile.
Larger batches are deliberately absent -- the kernel is faster
there in isolation, but the end-to-end serving measurement did not
reproduce a win, and a row is a promise about end-to-end
behaviour, not about the kernel alone.
